patterns.message: shared/ is the bottom of the stack: it may import shared/ and navigation/ and nothing else. A feature, a layout or the app importing shared/ is the intended direction; the reverse turns the kit into feature code. Move the shared piece down, or lift the feature's own piece up.
navigation/ describes where the pages are, not what they contain. It may import shared/ only. The router maps a nav item to its page — that lookup lives in app/router.tsx.

Reach another feature through its barrel — '../feedback', not '../feedback/FeedbackCard'. What a feature exports is its contract; everything else is free to change. If you need something that is not exported, add it to that feature's index.ts deliberately.
A feature must not import the shell or the app that mounts it — that is a cycle waiting to happen. Take what you need as a prop, or read the session with useAuth.
